key_insight: DARE-bench introduces a process-aware benchmark that measures both modeling quality and instruction/process fidelity of LLMs on multi-step data science tasks, plus a curated set of accurately labeled examples to enable reliable evaluation. It reveals gaps between surface-task performance and true adherence to prescribed data-science workflows.
problem_solved: Current LLM benchmarks for data science miss two things: they don't evaluate whether models follow multi-step instructions and internal reasoning/processes (process fidelity), and they lack high-quality, accurately labeled examples for training and evaluation. DARE-bench fills both gaps with standardized, process-aware metrics and a carefully curated dataset.
method: Design a benchmark suite of multi-step data science tasks that encode explicit workflows and evaluation checkpoints (data cleaning, feature engineering, modeling, evaluation, interpretation).
Define process-aware metrics that quantify instruction adherence and fidelity (e.g., step-by-step correctness, deviation from required procedures, and intermediate-output checks).
Provide a curated, accurately labeled dataset and evaluation protocols; run baseline evaluations across popular LLMs to demonstrate differences between surface accuracy and process fidelity.
impact: DARE-bench enables practitioners and researchers to more reliably assess whether LLMs not only produce correct answers but also follow required workflows—critical for reproducibility, safety, and deployment in data-science pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the multi-step data-science workflow (clean → feature → model → evaluate → interpret) with checkpoints for fidelity checks
Bar chart comparing model scores on standard accuracy vs process-fidelity metrics to highlight gaps
Example trace visualization (side-by-side) showing an LLM's stepwise outputs vs ground-truth process steps
Heatmap of instruction-adherence across tasks and models to identify consistent failure modes
paper_title: DARE-bench: Evaluating Modeling and Instruction Fidelity of LLMs in Data Science
paper_authors: Fan Shu, Yite Wang, Ruofan Wu, Boyi Liu, Zhewei Yao
